key_findings: **Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaControl** is the ENGINE-SIDE Lua control class. Single-inheritance per RTTI (CHD attributes=0, numBaseClasses=5). Ctor at FUN_00CCCB70 is just 16 bytes (vftable write + 1 field zero-init) - LuaControl is a barebones abstract base. 4 derived classes via ctor callers.

**Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control::StatusBase** is the SCRIPT-SIDE Lua status base. Multi-inheritance per RTTI (CHD attributes=1, numBaseClasses=11). Ctor + dtor pair at FUN_00776200 + FUN_00776270 (109 + 102 bytes). 2 vftables: PRIMARY @ 0x00FDF8D4 (object+0x00), SECONDARY @ 0x00FDF8DC (object+0x60).

**StatusBase INHERITS FROM LuaControl**: BCD pointer 0x0115CAB8 (LuaControl's own Base Class Descriptor) appears at array entry 2 of StatusBase's Base Class Array (0x0115F858). The 11 base classes of StatusBase include LuaControl as one of them, at offset 0 in the layout.

**The 2-tier Lua-bridge architecture for status state**: engine-side LuaControl (Component::Lua::GameEngine namespace, 5 base classes) + script-side StatusBase (Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control namespace, 11 base classes - inherits from LuaControl + 10 others). Concrete status classes (e.g. ActorSubStatStatus) derive from StatusBase, gaining both engine-side Lua-controllability AND script-side status semantics.

**FUN_00CC70E0 is a trivial 34-byte thunk** to FUN_00CD8050 (38 bytes) to FUN_00D03A50 (not decomped here). The +200000 offset reference from BCS-Y-1368's note was about a VALUE passed to the function, not the function body. This 3-level thunk chain is likely a CRT-emitted formatter or status-id transformer.

**LuaControl's 4 derived classes** are: FUN_0070A8A0, FUN_006DBB70, FUN_00CD8990, FUN_00712A90 (ctors of derived classes that call LuaControl::ctor). Note FUN_006DBB70 also appears as a callee from StatusBase::ctor's SEH frame setup - context-dependent role.

**StatusBase secondary vftable at +0x60 (=96)** corresponds to one of the 4 base classes in the RTTI Base Class Array at offsets 96/100 (BCDs at array entries 7-10). Could be a property-bag or change-notification interface - confirms multi-inheritance is REAL (not just template instantiation).

**Client-architecture 'The LuaControl hierarchy is the runtime surface' candidate** ('Bahamut status objects use a 2-tier Lua-bridge') is DEFERRED. Needs more evidence across the 7 other callers of FUN_00CC70E0 to confirm the pattern is universal across Receiver apply helpers.
